svg.title: One RF-DETR training step as a blueprint
svg.desc: A blueprint of one RF-DETR training step with a symbol that follows the data and changes with its type. Left, the data path from top to bottom: 1 the dataset on disk holds images with annotations and is unchanged; 2 augmentation applies a random set of transforms such as rotate, scale and flip to the image and moves the annotations with it, which changes pixels and boxes; 3 several augmented samples are composed into a float batch tensor of shape B, 3, H, W with a list of targets, which changes the format. The batch then forks: the images go to the network and the annotations go to the compare step. Right, the model: 4 the network reads its weights and turns the images into predictions; 5 the predictions are 300 boxes with class scores per image; 6 they are compared with the annotations, the ground truth; 7 the loss, class plus L1 plus GIoU, is one number for the batch. The loss goes back into the network only, as a gradient for every weight, with the norm clipped to 0.1, and the AdamW step then changes the weights and updates the EMA copy. Nothing goes back to the data. A side card lists the TrainConfig settings batch_size, multi_scale, grad_accum_steps, use_ema and aug_config. After the last batch the epoch validates without augmentation, computes COCO mAP, saves the best checkpoint and checks early stopping.
svg.text: One training step, drawn as a blueprint
Left: the data path. Right: the model. Follow the symbol; the half that is working is bright.

what the network answers for each image
L = class + L1 + GIoU, averaged over the batch
gradient dL/dw: back into the network, never into the data

svg.text: AFTER THE LAST BATCH OF THE EPOCH
Then the next epoch starts, or the run ends. Loggers get train/loss every step and val/* every epoch.
